items.title: AbCellera’s Menopause Drug Cuts Hot Flashes by 83% in Phase 2 Trial
items.body: AbCellera reported positive Phase 2 results for ABCL635, a long-acting, nonhormonal antibody treatment for hot flashes in postmenopausal women, causing stock prices to surge up to 41%. The biotech company’s study met its primary efficacy endpoints: reducing hot flash frequency and episode severity. Of the 92 postmenopausal women – who reported experiencing 10 moderate-to-severe hot flashes a day – those treated with… The post AbCellera’s Menopause Drug Cuts Hot Flashes by 83% in Phase 2 Trial first appeared on .
items.why: AbCellera reported Phase 2 trial results for ABCL635, a nonhormonal antibody treatment for menopausal hot flashes, showing the drug met its primary efficacy endpoints by reducing hot flash frequency and severity by up to 83% in 92 postmenopausal women, sending the company's stock up as much as 41%. This is a real clinical trial readout with concrete numbers and market impact, representing one of the more substantial industry developments in women's health this week.
items.plain: A biotech company announced strong results from a mid-stage clinical trial testing a new non-hormonal drug for menopause hot flashes, with symptoms dropping by as much as 83% in the 92 women studied, and the company's stock price jumped sharply as a result. This is a real medical and business milestone with actual trial numbers behind it, not just an announcement or plan.

glossary.definition: An early-to-mid stage clinical trial in a moderate number of patients that tests whether a treatment works and is reasonably safe, before larger confirmatory trials.
The main measurable outcome a clinical trial is designed to test in order to determine whether a treatment works.

items.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
items.body: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is a key prodromal marker of Parkinson's disease (PD). Video-polysomnography (vPSG) remains the diagnostic gold standard, but manual sleep staging is particularly time-consuming and challenging in neurodegenerative disease. We adapted U-Sleep, a deep neural network, for automated sleep staging in PD and iRBD. A pretrained model (PUB, 19,236 PSGs), was finetuned on multicenter datasets (PACE, CBC: 112 PD, 138 iRBD, 89 controls) and evaluated on a clinical hold-out (DCSM: 81 PD, 36 iRBD, 87 controls). Predictors of staging agreement were analyzed, and low-agreement recordings were blindly rescored. Confidence-based thresholds were applied to enhance REM detection. The pretrained model achieved κ = 0.66 in PACE/CBC, improving to κ = 0.74 after finetuning (p < 0.001). In the hold-out, mean κ increased from 0.60 to 0.64 (p < 0.001). Site-specific finetuning provided minimal benefit. Confidence was a significant predictor of Cohen's κ (p < 0.001). Recordings with low model agreement also showed low human interrater agreement. Applying a confidence threshold increased REM precision from 85 to 95.6%, preserving sufficient REM sleep in 96% of subjects. This publicly available model achieves human-level agreement enabling scalable, standardized PSG analysis with model-derived confidence as a tool for further refinements.
items.why: Researchers adapted U-Sleep, a deep neural network for automated sleep staging, and validated it across multicenter cohorts of Parkinson's disease (PD) and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) patients, finding agreement with human scorers (Cohen's kappa) rising from 0.60 to 0.74 after finetuning, with a confidence threshold boosting REM sleep detection precision from 85% to 95.6%. This is a rare example of a deep learning tool for polysomnography (PSG) staging tested on an external clinical hold-out set in a neurodegenerative population, making it a credible step toward scalable, standardized sleep analysis in this diagnostically difficult group.
items.plain: Scientists tested an AI system that automatically scores sleep stages from overnight sleep recordings, using it on patients with Parkinson's disease and a related sleep disorder that often precedes it. After training on data from multiple hospitals, the AI matched human experts closely and got much better at correctly flagging REM sleep, a stage crucial for diagnosis, when it used a confidence check on its own answers.

glossary.definition: A sleep disorder where people act out dreams during REM sleep, often an early warning sign of Parkinson's disease.
A progressive brain disorder that affects movement and is linked to loss of certain nerve cells.
An overnight test that records brain waves, breathing, and other signals to study sleep.
A type of computer program loosely modeled on the brain that learns patterns from large amounts of data.
A statistic that measures how much two raters or a rater and a model agree, correcting for agreement expected by chance.
A separate group of data, not used to train the model, that tests whether it works on new patients.

items.title: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Clinicians in Evidence-Based Cardiovascular Disease Management for People Living With HIV: Comparative Study.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Although widespread antiretroviral therapy has extended the life expectancy of people living with HIV, cardiovascular disease (CVD) has emerged as a primary comorbidity. Persistent cross-specialty knowledge gaps in routine clinical practice lead to suboptimal adherence to guidelines. Integrated, evidence-based tools are urgently needed to overcome these interdisciplinary barriers. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated significant capabilities in medicine, no systematic evaluation has assessed their ability to facilitate multidisciplinary CVD management for people living with HIV. OBJECTIVE: This study compared the performance of 4 mainstream AI models (DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, ChatGPT-4o, and ChatGPT-o4-mini) against 12 human clinicians (8 infectious disease specialists and 4 cardiologists) in addressing guideline-based CVD management tasks for people living with HIV. METHODS: Based on 4 authoritative domestic and international HIV/CVD guidelines, a structured 25-question assessment was developed via 2 rounds of Delphi consultation. Standard reference answers and an evaluation framework were finalized through expert consensus. LLM responses were generated using standardized prompts. Clinicians answered identical questions via one-on-one structured interviews, transcribed verbatim. Six multidisciplinary experts independently rated all responses across 4 dimensions-accuracy, completeness, readability, and reliability-using a 4-point ordinal scale (1=poor to 4=excellent). Cumulative link mixed models analyzed intergroup differences. RESULTS: All AI models achieved significantly higher scores than clinicians across all dimensions (P<.001). The AI group's mean scores ranged from 3.44 to 3.68 (median 4, IQR 3.0-4.0; coefficient of variation=0.145-0.178). Conversely, clinicians' scores were lower (mean 1.78-2.05; median 2, IQR 1.0-3.0; coefficient of variation=0.428-0.473) with marked dispersion. DeepSeek-R1 delivered the optimal performance, significantly outperforming the other 3 models (all P<.001). Specialty-stratified analysis revealed no significant overall score difference between cardiologists and infectious disease specialists (odds ratio 0.92, 95% CI 0.84-1.01; P=.09). However, dimension-specific analysis indicated that cardiologists scored higher in accuracy (odds ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.67-0.97; P=.03). Domain-specific divergence was evident: cardiologists outperformed infectious disease specialists in CVD risk assessment (2.26 vs 1.83), whereas infectious disease specialists led in drug adverse effect evaluation (2.23 vs 1.65). CONCLUSIONS: In this structured question-and-answer study, LLMs outperformed human clinicians across all metrics for HIV-associated CVD management, with DeepSeek-R1 achieving superior composite scores. These findings validate DeepSeek-R1's potential as a cross-disciplinary decision-support tool capable of integrating complex clinical knowledge, mitigating specialty gaps, and enhancing information precision. Integrating AI systems into multidisciplinary workflows, complemented by targeted clinical training, may optimize the management of complex comorbidities in people living with HIV.
items.why: In this comparative study, four large language models (LLMs, AI systems trained on huge amounts of text to generate human-like responses) were pitted against 12 human clinicians on 25 guideline-based questions about cardiovascular disease management in people with HIV, with blinded experts rating accuracy, completeness, readability, and reliability on a 4-point scale; the AI models scored significantly higher across all dimensions (P<.001), with DeepSeek-R1 performing best. This is a genuine head-to-head clinician comparison rather than a rubric-only chatbot evaluation, though the reader should note the assessment used structured interview questions rather than real patient interactions, limiting generalizability to bedside communication.
items.plain: Researchers compared four AI chatbots against 12 real doctors on answering 25 questions about heart disease care in HIV patients, and expert judges rated the AI answers as clearly better across accuracy, completeness, readability, and trustworthiness. This matters because it directly compares AI to real clinicians rather than just grading AI answers alone, though the questions were a structured test rather than real patient conversations.

glossary.definition: AI systems trained on huge amounts of text that can understand and generate human-like language.
A statistical measure indicating how likely a result could have occurred by chance alone, with smaller values suggesting a more reliable finding.

items.title: Role prompting modulates linguistic style but not clinical decision structure in GPT-5 tumour board simulation.
items.body: Multidisciplinary tumour boards (MDTs) are the standard for gastrointestinal oncological decision-making but remain resource-intensive. Whether specialty-specific role prompting induces genuinely distinct clinical reasoning in large language models (LLMs)-or merely role-appropriate language around an invariant output-has not been systematically tested. We applied five zero-shot prompting frameworks and a majority-vote ensemble to GPT-5 across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases with MDT-validated decisions: a simulated MDT, multi-expert deliberation, three specialist personas, and a majority-vote ensemble. Concordance with MDT recommendations ranged from 78% to 87%, with no significant inter-framework differences (Cochran's Q = 8.46, p = 0.133). Specialty-characteristic language was near-universal (97-100%) but uncorrelated with accuracy. Embedding analysis revealed high semantic similarity across personas (cosine similarity 0.805-0.836; η² = 0.049), contrasting with substantially greater output separation under multi-expert deliberation (η² = 0.554-0.581). GPT-5 reliably adapts linguistic style to clinical personas but produces limited specialty-specific output diversity, supporting its role as a decision-support adjunct rather than an autonomous specialist simulator.
items.why: In a zero-shot prompting experiment, GPT-5 (a large language model, LLM) was given five different specialist-persona and multi-expert deliberation frameworks across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases with multidisciplinary tumour board (MDT)-validated decisions, achieving 78-87% concordance with no significant difference between frameworks, while embedding analysis showed personas produced similar linguistic style but limited differences in underlying reasoning. This suggests role prompting mainly changes surface language rather than clinical judgment, a useful caution for anyone designing LLM-based decision-support tools that claim to simulate distinct specialist viewpoints.
items.plain: Researchers tested whether telling an AI chatbot to "act like" different medical specialists actually changes its medical advice, using 100 real cancer cases with known correct treatment decisions from real tumor boards. The AI matched the real experts about 80 percent of the time no matter which persona it was given, and while it changed its wording to sound like different specialists, its actual recommendations stayed nearly the same underneath.

glossary.definition: A meeting where doctors from different specialties jointly decide on a patient's cancer treatment.
A type of AI trained on large amounts of text that can generate humanlike written responses.
Giving an AI a task or instruction without first showing it worked examples of that exact task.
The degree to which two decisions, such as an AI's and a human panel's, agree with each other.
A way of measuring how similar two pieces of text are in meaning by converting them into numerical representations and comparing those numbers.

items.title: Impact of AI-Augmented informed consent on preoperative anxiety and patient understanding: A prospective Observational Study.
items.body: OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated the clinical integration of a large language model (LLM) as a supportive communication tool within the preoperative informed consent pathway. METHODS: Participants completed the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI)-1, STAI-2, and Amsterdam Preoperative Anxiety and Information Scale (APAIS) scales after undergoing both the standard informed consent process and the subsequent ChatGPT consultation. Additionally, they completed a five-item questionnaire to assess their experience with the digital consultation. Anxiety scores were statistically compared before and after the AI consultation. Patient satisfaction regarding the digital consultation process was analyzed. Additionally, ChatGPT's responses to the eleven most frequently asked questions were evaluated by three independent urologists in terms of accuracy, comprehensibility, and appropriateness. RESULTS: Anxiety scores decreased significantly. STAI-1 decreased by 3.2 points and STAI-2 by 1.3 points (both p<0.001). ROC analysis identified minimal clinically significant difference (MCID) thresholds of 1.5 for STAI-1 and 0.5 for STAI-2, indicating that these reductions were clinically significant. In contrast, APAIS scores decreased by 0.89 points (p < 0.001), but the ROC analysis was not significant (AUC = 0.559, p = 0.327), suggesting limited clinical relevance. Subgroup analyses showed that reductions in STAI scores generally exceeded the MCID thresholds, whereas APAIS changes did not consistently achieve clinical meaningfulness. Most participants reported that the ChatGPT consultation contributed to their understanding of the surgery (68%). CONCLUSION: LLM-assisted consultation may serve as a scalable adjunct to clinician-led consent by enhancing perioperative communication and reducing situational anxiety, while requiring continued clinical oversight for safe implementation.
items.why: This prospective observational study integrated a large language model (LLM), ChatGPT, into the preoperative informed consent pathway and measured its effect on validated anxiety scales, finding a statistically and clinically significant reduction in State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) state anxiety scores, with 68% of patients reporting improved surgical understanding. This is a genuine measured effect on patient anxiety and understanding from real clinical integration, which meets the bar for this beat, though it lacks a comparator group receiving only standard consent and used urologist raters rather than blinded assessment.
items.plain: Doctors added an AI chatbot conversation after the normal informed consent process before surgery, and measured whether it changed patients' anxiety levels using standard psychological questionnaires. Anxiety went down by an amount doctors consider meaningful, and most patients said the chatbot helped them understand the surgery better, though the study did not compare against a group of patients who skipped the chatbot step entirely.

glossary.definition: A type of AI trained on large amounts of text that can generate humanlike written responses.
A widely used questionnaire that measures a person's current anxiety level and their general tendency toward anxiety.
A study that follows participants forward in time and records what happens, without the researchers assigning who gets which treatment.

items.title: Performance and limitations of four large language models in genetic counseling for thalassemia.
items.body: In regions with high thalassemia prevalence, such as southern China and Southeast Asia, chronic shortages of professional genetic counseling resources have driven interest in large language models (LLMs) as auxiliary tools, yet their performance and safety boundaries in this setting remain uncharacterized. This single-center retrospective study evaluated four LLMs (ChatGPT-5.2 Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2 chat, Gemini 3 Flash, and Grok 4.1 Fast) using 1,080 standardized knowledge questions administered across five independent sessions and 150 real-world clinical cases scored by six senior experts across eight dimensions. All models exceeded 90% accuracy on single-choice and true-false questions. Between-model differences were most pronounced in multiple-choice questions, where ChatGPT-5.2 Thinking achieved the highest accuracy (87.28% ± 1.69%), significantly outperforming Grok 4.1 Fast (72.06% ± 1.69%, < 0.001). DeepSeek-V3.2 chat showed lower cross-session consistency than the other three models. In clinical case analysis, all models scored below human expert levels overall, with ChatGPT-5.2 Thinking performing closest to experts. Test report interpretation was generally adequate, whereas larger gaps emerged in genetic risk estimation, phenotype prediction, and counseling recommendations (all < 0.001 vs. human experts, with limited exceptions for ChatGPT-5.2 Thinking in-thalassemia subtypes). All 145 severe errors were confined to-thalassemia and-combined--thalassemia subtypes, concentrated in phenotype prediction (76/145, 52.4%) and risk estimation (40/145, 27.6%). LLMs may support knowledge retrieval and structured report interpretation in thalassemia genetic counseling but should not be used independently for risk assessment or final counseling decisions, particularly in complex-related cases.
items.why: This retrospective study evaluated four large language models (LLMs) on standardized thalassemia genetic counseling knowledge questions and 150 real-world clinical cases scored by six senior experts, finding all models exceeded 90% accuracy on structured knowledge questions but scored below human expert level on clinical case analysis, with 145 severe errors concentrated in phenotype prediction and risk estimation. This provides a genuine expert-benchmarked comparison revealing a specific, clinically important failure mode, namely unreliable genetic risk estimation, that is directly relevant to evaluating LLMs for patient-facing counseling tasks.
items.plain: Researchers tested four AI chatbots on genetic counseling questions and real patient cases related to thalassemia, a blood disorder, comparing their answers to those of experienced genetic counselors. The chatbots did well on simple factual questions but fell short of human experts on real cases, especially when predicting how severe a patient's disease might be or estimating genetic risk, showing a specific area where these tools are not yet safe to rely on alone.

glossary.definition: A type of AI trained on large amounts of text that can generate humanlike written responses.
A study design that looks back at existing cases or data rather than following new patients forward in time.
Predicting the observable characteristics or symptoms a person will have based on their genetic makeup.

items.title: Finite State Machine-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation Improves Expert-Rated Acceptability of a Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter Self-Management Chatbot: Single-Center Content Validation Study.
items.body: BACKGROUND: Patients with cancer undergoing long-term or vesicant chemotherapy frequently require peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs). Due to the nature of ambulatory treatment administration, self-PICC management is essential for the continuation and completion of the planned treatment. Large language models offer potential for continuous patient support, but hallucinations and insufficient adherence to clinical protocols remain concerns. Fine-tuning (FT) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improve factual grounding but cannot enforce the structured decision logic of expert-led PICC consultations, leaving the value of dialogue-control mechanisms unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study is an expert-panel evaluation designed to exploratorily verify whether a finite state machine (FSM)-guided RAG architecture yields incremental gains in clinical acceptability when added on top of FT and RAG compared with simpler architectures (fine-tuned model alone; fine-tuned model with RAG). METHODS: We conducted a blinded ablation comparison of three chatbot architectures sharing an identical fine-tuned GPT-4o-mini base: model 1 (fine-tuning only; FT), model 2 (FT + RAG), and model 3 (FT + RAG + FSM). Three nurses specializing in PICC management (≥10 y experience) independently evaluated responses to 43 PICC-related queries. The two-stage evaluation comprised query-level forced-choice preference and global Likert ratings across 8 predefined dimensions. Interrater agreement was quantified with Gwet AC1. Preference rates were compared with Cochran Q and pairwise McNemar tests with Bonferroni correction. Global Likert ratings were summarized descriptively across 8 predefined dimensions. RESULTS: The FSM-guided model (model 3) was preferred in 34 of 43 scenarios (79.1%). Interrater agreement was moderate (Gwet AC1=0.58, 95% CI 0.42-0.75; P<.001). Differences in model preference were significant (Cochran Q=48.2; P<.001). Pairwise McNemar tests showed model 3 was preferred significantly more often than model 1 and model 2 (both P<.001), while model 1 versus model 2 did not differ after Bonferroni correction. For the global ratings, descriptive statistics indicated that model 3 received higher ratings than models 1 and 2 across most criteria, although it tended to receive lower ratings for efficiency, possibly reflecting its multiturn structure. In qualitative debriefing, the nurses noted occasional unnecessary conversational turns under FSM guidance. CONCLUSIONS: In this expert-panel content-validation study, the FSM-guided fine-tuned RAG model received higher expert-rated acceptability than the simpler architectures, with FSM-based dialogue control more closely aligning chatbot outputs with expert-led PICC consultation patterns. Patient-facing usability testing and multicenter validation are required before claims regarding patient safety or clinical deployment can be made.
items.why: This single-center content validation study compared three chatbot architectures for a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) self-management tool, finding that adding a finite state machine (FSM)-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) layer on top of fine-tuning and standard RAG was preferred by expert nurses in 79.1% of 43 clinical query scenarios, a statistically significant improvement over simpler architectures. This is a real comparative evaluation with clinician raters and a plausible deployment target, revealing both a benefit of structured dialogue control and a specific tradeoff of reduced conversational efficiency, which is directly useful to this reader's interest in chatbot design for patient-facing tasks.
items.plain: Researchers built three versions of a chatbot meant to help cancer patients manage a type of long-term IV line at home, each with a different level of built-in structure and rule-following, and had experienced nurses judge which one gave the best answers to real patient questions. The most structured version was clearly preferred by the nurses most of the time, though it sometimes took more back-and-forth to get an answer, showing a specific design choice that improves AI reliability for patient self-care instructions but at some cost to speed.

glossary.definition: A thin, long tube inserted into a vein in the arm and threaded to a larger vein near the heart, used for long-term delivery of medications like chemotherapy.
A method where an AI language model first looks up relevant documents or data before writing its answer, aiming to make responses more accurate and grounded.
A process of further training an already-built AI model on a smaller, specific set of data to make it better at a particular task.
A system design that follows a fixed set of defined steps or states, moving between them based on specific rules, used here to keep a chatbot's conversation on a structured path.

items.title: Oura Seeks Patent To Detect Pregnancy Complications
items.body: Oura is seeking to patent a pulse wave velocity system designed to detect pregnancy complications earlier, per Wareable, adding another layer to its expanding women’s health strategy. The system would continuously track blood pressure and arterial stiffness, flagging abnormal changes that could signal hypertension, preeclampsia, and gestational diabetes. The company did not comment on the filing. The patent marks Oura’s latest move into… The post Oura Seeks Patent To Detect Pregnancy Complications first appeared on .
items.why: Wearable company Oura is seeking a patent for a pulse wave velocity system intended to continuously monitor blood pressure and arterial stiffness to flag early signs of preeclampsia, hypertension, and gestational diabetes. A patent filing from an established, well-funded consumer health company signals a concrete step toward a new pregnancy-monitoring capability, even though it has not yet been built or validated.
items.plain: Oura, the company known for its health-tracking ring, is trying to patent a way to continuously watch blood pressure and blood vessel stiffness to catch pregnancy complications like preeclampsia earlier. This is a real move by a major company toward a new pregnancy health feature, though it is still just a patent application, not a finished or tested product.

items.title: Perimenopause Platform Play Health Shuts Down
items.body: Perimenopause platform Play Health is shutting down, Co-Founder and CEO Andrea Mazzocchi, announced on LinkedIn. Launched in 2025, Play Health offered patients a place to track their symptoms, medications, cycles, and habits between appointments, generating AI-assisted personalized care plans and insights for their providers. As Mazzocchi put it,, Play Health’s “goal was to make personalized menopause care accessible to women by giving… The post Perimenopause Platform Play Health Shuts Down first appeared on .
items.why: Perimenopause tracking and care-planning platform Play Health, launched in 2025, announced it is shutting down according to its CEO. Company failures are meaningful signal in this beat about market viability and sustainability of AI-assisted personalized care models in women's health.
items.plain: A startup that used AI to help track menopause symptoms and create personalized care plans is closing down after only about a year. This kind of failure is useful to know because it shows which business models in women's health are struggling to survive.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Multimodal Ultrasound Model for Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Development and Validation.
items.body: OBJECTIVES: The primary aim of this study was to develop a multimodal artificial intelligence model for predicting spontaneous preterm birth using cervical 2-dimensional ultrasound and elastography images, as well as ultrasound parameters. METHODS: This prospective cohort study recruited pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound screening at 20-24 weeks of gestation. Participants were divided into spontaneous preterm birth group and full-term group. Three deep learning models were trained on images to compute scores via the best-performing model. Five supervised machine learning classifiers were developed and validated to predict spontaneous preterm birth based on ultrasound parameters and deep learning scores, and feature importance analysis was employed to visualize the importance of each feature in the model. RESULTS: A total of 721 pregnant women (44 with spontaneous preterm birth) were included. In deep learning models based on ultrasound images, DenseNet121 (AUC: 0.92/0.93) model exhibited excellent performance, and corresponding scores were obtained. Elasticity contrast index, hardness ratio, external os stiffness, Ratio, 2-dimension-score, and elastography-score were included to construct the 5 machine learning models. Among the multimodal models, the neural network model showed the best predictive performance in the validation set (AUC = 0.85; 95% CI, 0.73-0.96). Feature importance analysis revealed that both elastography-score and 2-dimension-score made significant contributions in a majority of the models. CONCLUSIONS: The multimodal artificial intelligence models using ultrasound parameters and cervical 2-dimensional ultrasound and elastography images demonstrated promising predictive capabilities in internal validation for spontaneous preterm birth in the second trimester. This offers assistance for intervention in patients at high risk of spontaneous preterm birth.
items.why: In a prospective cohort of 721 pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound at 20-24 weeks, a multimodal deep learning model combining cervical 2D ultrasound, elastography images, and clinical parameters predicted spontaneous preterm birth, with the best neural network achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.85 on internal validation. The study used a real prospective design and reasonable sample size but relied only on internal validation with a small number of preterm cases (44), limiting confidence that the result will generalize to other settings.
items.plain: Researchers built an AI system that combines several types of ultrasound images and measurements of a pregnant woman's cervix to predict whether she will deliver prematurely, testing it on over 700 pregnant women. The system correctly separated at-risk from not-at-risk women fairly well, but it was only tested on the same group of patients it was built from, not confirmed on an outside group.

glossary.term: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC)
glossary.definition: A number between 0.5 and 1 that measures how well a model distinguishes between people who will and will not have an outcome, where 1 is perfect and 0.5 is no better than chance.
A group of participants followed forward in time from the start of a study, rather than looking back at existing records.
An imaging technique that measures the stiffness of tissue, which can indicate physical changes relevant to disease or pregnancy risk.
Testing a model's performance on a portion of the same dataset it was built from, as opposed to testing it on entirely separate data.

terms.definition: A measure comparing the risk of an event over time between two groups, adjusted for other factors, where a value above 1 means higher risk.
Measures of privacy risk calculated across an entire dataset rather than for each individual person.
A hormone produced by ovarian follicles that is commonly used to estimate a woman's remaining egg supply.
The tendency for an initial piece of information, like a first guess, to unduly influence a person's final judgment.
Having an abnormal number of chromosomes, which often prevents an embryo from developing successfully.
A single number from 0.5 to 1 that summarizes how well a test distinguishes between two groups, with 1 meaning perfect separation and 0.5 meaning no better than chance.

terms.term: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC-ROC)
terms.definition: A measure from 0.5 to 1 of how well a model distinguishes between two outcomes across all possible decision thresholds, with 1 being perfect and 0.5 being no better than chance.

terms.term: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC)
terms.definition: A number between 0.5 and 1 that measures how well a model distinguishes between people who will and will not have an outcome, where 1 is perfect and 0.5 is no better than chance.

terms.term: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (ROC-AUC)
terms.definition: A number from 0 to 1 that measures how well a model can tell apart two groups, such as patients who will versus won't develop a condition, with 1 being perfect and 0.5 being no better than chance.
Medical procedures used to help people conceive, such as in vitro fertilization.
A single number from 0 to 1 summarizing how well a model distinguishes people with and without a condition, where 1 is perfect and 0.5 is no better than guessing.
A number from 0.5 to 1 summarizing how well a model distinguishes between two outcomes across all possible decision thresholds, with 1 being perfect and 0.5 being no better than chance.
The tendency for people to over-trust an automated system's output, even when it may be wrong.
A way of measuring how correct a model is that gives equal weight to its performance on both positive and negative cases, useful when one outcome is much rarer than the other.
An early-stage embryo, several days after fertilization, that is ready for genetic testing or transfer to the uterus.
A study design feature where evaluators do not know which responses came from which source, reducing bias in judging quality.

How well a model's predicted probabilities match the real-world frequency of the outcome it is predicting.

Software that gives doctors extra information or suggestions to help them make better medical decisions, without replacing their judgment.

A machine learning technique that trains a model by teaching it to recognize which examples are similar or different from each other.
Repeating an analysis using a separate group of people measured at a single point in time, to see if the original finding holds up.

A type of computer program loosely modeled on the brain that learns patterns from large amounts of data.

A single number combining sensitivity and specificity that summarizes how well a test distinguishes between people with and without a condition, where higher values mean better discrimination.
An imaging technique that detects how water molecules move through tissue, which can reveal information about tissue structure and blood flow.
The length of time after treatment that a patient survives without their disease coming back.
A chemical modification to DNA that can turn genes on or off without changing the underlying genetic code, and that changes with age.
An advanced statistical technique that uses machine learning to estimate causal effects while reducing bias from imperfect models, making the results more reliable than simpler methods.

The US Food and Drug Administration, the government agency that reviews and approves medical products including software as a medical device.

The fluid surrounding an egg inside its follicle in the ovary, which contains molecules reflecting the egg's environment.
The FDA is the US government agency that reviews and approves drugs, devices, and some software for safety and effectiveness before they can be sold.

A statistical measure of how much results vary across different studies being combined, where high heterogeneity means the studies do not agree well with each other.
A category of moderately to severely abnormal cervical cells that carries meaningful risk of progressing to cervical cancer if untreated.

terms.term: High-grade Squamous Intraepithelial Lesions or Worse (HSIL+)

A portion of data set aside and not used during model training, so it can be used afterward to test how well the model performs on new cases.

Heparan sulfate proteoglycan 2, also called Perlecan, a structural protein found in the extracellular matrix that helps form tissue scaffolding.

A group of genetic eye conditions that damage the light-sensing layer at the back of the eye, often leading to vision loss.

A statistic that measures how closely two sets of measurements, such as two raters or a model and a rater, agree with each other.

AI systems trained on huge amounts of text that can understand and generate human-like language.

Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME), a technique that explains an individual AI prediction by approximating the model's behavior with a simpler, interpretable one nearby.
A method of preparing cervical cell samples on slides by suspending them in liquid before examination, which improves sample clarity compared to older smear techniques.
A method of preparing cervical cell samples in liquid rather than smearing them directly on a slide, which produces clearer samples for microscopic review.
A study that follows the same people over time to see how something changes.
A birth weight below 2,500 grams, which is associated with higher risk of illness and death in newborns.

A method where computer programs improve their predictions by learning patterns from large amounts of data rather than following fixed rules.
A branch of AI in which computer models learn patterns from data rather than being explicitly programmed with rules.

A research approach that combines numerical data, such as survey scores, with descriptive information, such as interview or open-ended feedback.
A study design where the people rating the outputs do not know which AI system produced each answer, reducing bias in judging quality.
Relating to how an embryo's shape and structure change over time, as observed through continuous time-lapse imaging.
A study that analyzes previously collected data from multiple hospitals or sites, rather than following new patients forward in time.
A meeting where doctors from different specialties jointly decide on a cancer patient's treatment plan.
A meeting where doctors from different specialties jointly decide on a patient's cancer treatment.
A basic type of artificial neural network made of layers of connected nodes that learns to map inputs to outputs.
An MRI scan that captures several different types of image contrast from the same body region to give a fuller picture of tissue characteristics.
A study design where cases of a disease are compared to matched controls drawn from within a larger group being followed over time.
A visual scoring tool that combines multiple risk factors to estimate an individual patient's probability of an outcome.
A magnetic resonance imaging scan performed without injecting a contrast dye, making it safer and more accessible for patients with kidney problems or limited resources.
A statistical measure indicating how likely a result could have occurred by chance alone, with smaller values suggesting a more reliable finding.
A progressive brain disorder that affects movement and is linked to loss of certain nerve cells.
A protein on cells that can suppress the immune system, and a common target of cancer immunotherapy drugs.
A thin, long tube inserted into a vein in the arm and threaded to a larger vein near the heart, used for long-term delivery of medications like chemotherapy.
An early-to-mid stage clinical trial in a moderate number of patients that tests whether a treatment works and is reasonably safe, before larger confirmatory trials.
Predicting the observable characteristics or symptoms a person will have based on their genetic makeup.
Physician-in-the-loop (PITL), a validation approach where doctors actively review and judge an AI system's outputs as part of testing it, rather than the AI being evaluated purely by statistics.
An overnight recording of brain waves, breathing, and other body signals used to diagnose sleep disorders.
An overnight test that records brain waves, breathing, and other signals to study sleep.
Of the cases a model labels positive, the fraction that are actually correct, a measure of how trustworthy a positive call is.
A performance measure similar to ROC-AUC but more sensitive to how well a model finds rare positive cases specifically.
A pregnancy complication involving high blood pressure and organ damage that can be dangerous for both mother and baby.
A lab test performed on embryos before transfer that checks whether they have the normal number of chromosomes.
Doctors who provide general, first-contact medical care rather than specialized care.
The main measurable outcome a clinical trial is designed to test in order to determine whether a treatment works.
The length of time during and after treatment that a patient lives without their disease getting worse.
The length of time during and after treatment that a patient lives without their disease getting worse.
A group of participants followed forward in time from the start of a study, rather than looking back at existing records.
A study that enrolls participants and follows them forward in time to observe who develops an outcome of interest.
Research that follows the same participants forward in time, collecting data at multiple points, rather than looking backward at existing records.
A study that follows participants forward in time and records what happens, without the researchers assigning who gets which treatment.
A nine-item rating scale used to judge the quality of a clinical documentation summary across dimensions like accuracy, organization, and usefulness.
A technique that extracts detailed numerical patterns from medical images beyond what the eye can easily see.
A machine learning method that combines many decision trees, each trained on random subsets of data, to make a more stable overall prediction.
A study where participants are randomly assigned to different treatments or conditions so the results can be fairly compared.
A study where participants are randomly assigned to different treatments or interventions, which helps ensure fair comparison and reduces bias.
A large AI model pretrained on many retinal images that other researchers can adapt for specific eye-disease tasks, similar to starting with a knowledgeable foundation rather than from scratch.
A method where an AI language model first looks up relevant documents or data before writing its answer, aiming to make responses more accurate and grounded.
A study design that looks back at existing past data rather than collecting new data as events happen.
A study that reviews existing, already-collected records after the fact, rather than following patients forward in time.
A study design that looks back at existing cases or data rather than following new patients forward in time.
A study that looks back at existing patient records, but importantly tests its findings on a separate group of patients not used to build the model.
The absolute difference in the chance of an outcome between two groups, for example the percentage point gap in preterm birth rates between treated and untreated women.
The percentage of true positive cases that a test or model correctly identifies.
A ratio of two proteins measured in blood, soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 and placental growth factor, used clinically to help assess risk of preeclampsia.
A blood test measuring two proteins used to help predict preeclampsia risk in pregnancy.
A method that shows which input features most influenced a machine learning model's decision, making the model's reasoning easier to interpret.
A mathematical technique that assigns credit to each input feature for how much it contributed to a machine learning model's specific prediction, used to make AI decisions more understandable.
A technology that maps where different proteins are located within tissue, preserving the spatial arrangement of cells.
The percentage of true negative cases that a test or model correctly identifies as negative.
A machine learning approach that combines predictions from several different models into one final, usually more accurate, prediction.
An AI approach that combines predictions from several different models into one final, hopefully more accurate, prediction.
A widely used questionnaire that measures a person's current anxiety level and their general tendency toward anxiety.
A method that creates artificial extra examples of a rare outcome in a dataset so a model sees more of them during training.
A type of deep learning model designed specifically to work with tabular data, like spreadsheets of patient information, while also explaining which factors influenced its predictions.
Testing a model on data collected in a later time period than the data used to build it, to check that the model still works as circumstances or patient populations change over time.
A looser measure of correctness where the model's answer counts as right if the true answer appears anywhere among its five best guesses, rather than requiring the single top guess to be correct.
A method of evaluating a model by dividing data into one portion used to build the model and a separate portion used only to check its performance.
A type of AI architecture, originally developed for language processing, that can also be applied to other kinds of structured data to find complex patterns.
The idea of applying a result found in one study population to predict what would happen in a different population, and testing whether that transfer actually works.
A standardized clinical questionnaire and exam used to measure the severity of motor, cognitive, and behavioral symptoms in Huntington's disease.
A standard clinical scoring system used by doctors to measure the severity of symptoms in Huntington's disease.
A computer method that groups data points into clusters based on similarity, without being told the correct answer in advance.
A type of AI model designed to analyze images, often by breaking them into patches and learning patterns across the whole image.
A pretrained AI model that learns useful representations of raw audio, often reused as a building block in speech analysis systems.
Very high resolution digital scans of entire microscope slides used to examine tissue samples.
Asking an AI to perform a task without giving it any worked examples first, relying only on its existing training.
The ability of an AI model to correctly label or classify new data it was never specifically trained on.
Giving an AI a task or instruction without first showing it worked examples of that exact task.

scored.title: AbCellera’s Menopause Drug Cuts Hot Flashes by 83% in Phase 2 Trial
scored.why: AbCellera reported Phase 2 trial results for ABCL635, a nonhormonal antibody treatment for menopausal hot flashes, showing the drug met its primary efficacy endpoints by reducing hot flash frequency and severity by up to 83% in 92 postmenopausal women, sending the company's stock up as much as 41%. This is a real clinical trial readout with concrete numbers and market impact, representing one of the more substantial industry developments in women's health this week.

scored.title: Fully-automated sleep staging for Parkinson's disease and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
scored.why: Researchers adapted U-Sleep, a deep neural network for automated sleep staging, and validated it across multicenter cohorts of Parkinson's disease (PD) and isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) patients, finding agreement with human scorers (Cohen's kappa) rising from 0.60 to 0.74 after finetuning, with a confidence threshold boosting REM sleep detection precision from 85% to 95.6%. This is a rare example of a deep learning tool for polysomnography (PSG) staging tested on an external clinical hold-out set in a neurodegenerative population, making it a credible step toward scalable, standardized sleep analysis in this diagnostically difficult group.

scored.title: Comparative Performance of AI Models and Clinicians in Evidence-Based Cardiovascular Disease Management for People Living With HIV: Comparative Study.
scored.why: In this comparative study, four large language models (LLMs, AI systems trained on huge amounts of text to generate human-like responses) were pitted against 12 human clinicians on 25 guideline-based questions about cardiovascular disease management in people with HIV, with blinded experts rating accuracy, completeness, readability, and reliability on a 4-point scale; the AI models scored significantly higher across all dimensions (P<.001), with DeepSeek-R1 performing best. This is a genuine head-to-head clinician comparison rather than a rubric-only chatbot evaluation, though the reader should note the assessment used structured interview questions rather than real patient interactions, limiting generalizability to bedside communication.

scored.title: Role prompting modulates linguistic style but not clinical decision structure in GPT-5 tumour board simulation.
scored.why: In a zero-shot prompting experiment, GPT-5 (a large language model, LLM) was given five different specialist-persona and multi-expert deliberation frameworks across 100 gastrointestinal oncology cases with multidisciplinary tumour board (MDT)-validated decisions, achieving 78-87% concordance with no significant difference between frameworks, while embedding analysis showed personas produced similar linguistic style but limited differences in underlying reasoning. This suggests role prompting mainly changes surface language rather than clinical judgment, a useful caution for anyone designing LLM-based decision-support tools that claim to simulate distinct specialist viewpoints.

scored.title: Impact of AI-Augmented informed consent on preoperative anxiety and patient understanding: A prospective Observational Study.
scored.why: This prospective observational study integrated a large language model (LLM), ChatGPT, into the preoperative informed consent pathway and measured its effect on validated anxiety scales, finding a statistically and clinically significant reduction in State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) state anxiety scores, with 68% of patients reporting improved surgical understanding. This is a genuine measured effect on patient anxiety and understanding from real clinical integration, which meets the bar for this beat, though it lacks a comparator group receiving only standard consent and used urologist raters rather than blinded assessment.

scored.title: Performance and limitations of four large language models in genetic counseling for thalassemia.
scored.why: This retrospective study evaluated four large language models (LLMs) on standardized thalassemia genetic counseling knowledge questions and 150 real-world clinical cases scored by six senior experts, finding all models exceeded 90% accuracy on structured knowledge questions but scored below human expert level on clinical case analysis, with 145 severe errors concentrated in phenotype prediction and risk estimation. This provides a genuine expert-benchmarked comparison revealing a specific, clinically important failure mode, namely unreliable genetic risk estimation, that is directly relevant to evaluating LLMs for patient-facing counseling tasks.

scored.title: Finite State Machine-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation Improves Expert-Rated Acceptability of a Peripherally Inserted Central Catheter Self-Management Chatbot: Single-Center Content Validation Study.
scored.why: This single-center content validation study compared three chatbot architectures for a peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) self-management tool, finding that adding a finite state machine (FSM)-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) layer on top of fine-tuning and standard RAG was preferred by expert nurses in 79.1% of 43 clinical query scenarios, a statistically significant improvement over simpler architectures. This is a real comparative evaluation with clinician raters and a plausible deployment target, revealing both a benefit of structured dialogue control and a specific tradeoff of reduced conversational efficiency, which is directly useful to this reader's interest in chatbot design for patient-facing tasks.

scored.title: Oura Seeks Patent To Detect Pregnancy Complications
scored.why: Wearable company Oura is seeking a patent for a pulse wave velocity system intended to continuously monitor blood pressure and arterial stiffness to flag early signs of preeclampsia, hypertension, and gestational diabetes. A patent filing from an established, well-funded consumer health company signals a concrete step toward a new pregnancy-monitoring capability, even though it has not yet been built or validated.

scored.title: Perimenopause Platform Play Health Shuts Down
scored.why: Perimenopause tracking and care-planning platform Play Health, launched in 2025, announced it is shutting down according to its CEO. Company failures are meaningful signal in this beat about market viability and sustainability of AI-assisted personalized care models in women's health.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Multimodal Ultrasound Model for Prediction of Spontaneous Preterm Birth: Development and Validation.
scored.why: In a prospective cohort of 721 pregnant women undergoing transvaginal ultrasound at 20-24 weeks, a multimodal deep learning model combining cervical 2D ultrasound, elastography images, and clinical parameters predicted spontaneous preterm birth, with the best neural network achieving an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.85 on internal validation. The study used a real prospective design and reasonable sample size but relied only on internal validation with a small number of preterm cases (44), limiting confidence that the result will generalize to other settings.

scored.title: Accelerated Biological Age as an Early Pregnancy Risk Factor for Preeclampsia.
scored.why: Using LASSO regression and Random Forest on DNA methylation data from two prospective cohorts, this study identified accelerated biological aging via Hannum's epigenetic clock as a predictor of preeclampsia, validated with leave-one-out cross-validation logistic regression models in both cohorts. The consistent replication across two independent cohorts strengthens the biomarker signal, though the study remains a biomarker discovery effort without external validation in a distinct population or clinical deployment.

scored.title: Predicting Breast Cancer with Super-Resolution Ultrasound-Based Radiomics: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
scored.why: This multicenter retrospective study developed a radiomics model combining B-mode and super-resolution ultrasound (SRUS) features with clinical data to distinguish benign from malignant breast lesions, achieving an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.921 in training and 0.872 in an external validation cohort across 12 hospitals. The external validation and multicenter design make this a reasonably robust general clinical AI imaging study, though it addresses breast cancer diagnosis rather than reproductive medicine specifically.

scored.title: Large Language Model Simplification of Open Access Pediatric Strabismus Literature: Cross-Sectional Validation of Readability and Clinical Fidelity.
scored.why: This cross-sectional study used the large language model (LLM) DeepSeek-V3 to simplify 85 pediatric strabismus articles, reducing reading grade level by about 8 grades (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level from 15.79 to 7.84) while maintaining good clinical fidelity in 95% of summaries as rated by two specialists. This demonstrates a measurable, expert-validated improvement in patient education material quality, though it lacks a comparison to human-written simplifications or actual patient comprehension outcomes.

scored.title: Next Phase Femtech Launches With €1.6M to Advance Women’s Health
scored.why: A Danish-Swedish initiative called Next Phase Femtech launched with 1.6 million euros in EU regional funding to bring three named market-ready menopause solutions, including an AI-assisted symptom management app, closer to commercialization. This is specific funding tied to named products moving toward market, meeting the bar for a solid but not exceptional industry item.

scored.title: Papcup and Peripear Secure £75K Innovate UK Grant
scored.why: Women's health startups Papcup and Peripear each received 75,000 pounds in non-dilutive funding from Innovate UK's Women in Innovation program, with Papcup developing an at-home menstrual blood biosensor for detecting iron deficiency and cervical cancer. The funding is specific and tied to a described product with early data, but the amount is small and the technology unproven at scale.

scored.title: Placental Blood-Flow Velocity Quantification From Diffusion MRI.
scored.why: This methods study combined Monte Carlo simulations with machine learning regressors, random forest (RF) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), to estimate placental capillary blood velocity from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI), outperforming standard intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) methods on simulated data and producing physiologically plausible in vivo estimates. It is an early-stage technical validation without patient outcome data, but it addresses an important imaging gap relevant to preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction that could eventually inform obstetric risk prediction.

scored.title: Automated early preterm detection using hybrid multimodal attention network with gated fusion.
scored.why: This study built a hybrid deep learning model combining multi-head attention and gated fusion on electrohysterography (EHG) signals from 452 pregnancies to detect preterm labor earlier than the standard one-week window, reporting very high performance (accuracy 0.98, AUC 0.99). The near-perfect metrics from what appears to be a single-cohort study without mention of external validation raise concern about overfitting, limiting confidence that this would generalize to new clinical settings.

scored.title: AI Simplification of Dermatopathology Reports for Patients: Basic Versus Prompt-Engineered Approaches.
scored.why: This survey-based study had 52 dermatology and dermatopathology professionals rate AI-simplified dermatopathology reports generated by basic ChatGPT prompting versus a custom prompt-engineered tool, finding the custom tool performed no better and sometimes worse on completeness and harm ratings for certain conditions. This identifies a concrete failure mode where more elaborate prompting did not improve, and sometimes worsened, patient-facing simplification quality, though it used fictitious reports and professional raters rather than actual patients.

scored.title: Quality of nutrition information for breast cancer: A mixed-methods analysis of online information.
scored.why: This mixed-methods study analyzed nutrition-related claims for breast cancer patients across social media platforms, Google, and ChatGPT, finding fewer than 13% of 151 extracted claims were supported by reliable evidence, with Google and ChatGPT being relatively more accurate than social platforms like TikTok and Pinterest. This provides a useful, if narrow, data point on the comparative accuracy of AI chat output versus other online sources for patient-facing health information, but it lacks a clinician comparator or measured patient outcome.

scored.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of the readability of large language models for patient education on ophthalmological conditions.
scored.why: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 11 studies to compare readability of ChatGPT-generated patient education materials (PEMs) against existing clinician- or organization-authored ophthalmology materials, finding no significant difference in mean Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL) scores (9.82 vs 9.54, mean difference 0.21, 95% CI -1.52 to 1.94). The quantitative synthesis across many studies adds some rigor over a single readability study, but it still lacks a clinician-performance comparator or patient outcome measure, keeping it in the routine tier for this beat.

scored.title: Willow Partners With Providence Saint John’s To Expand Postpartum Support
scored.why: Maternal health company Willow launched a Hospital Partnership Program at Providence Saint John's Health Center, donating breastfeeding care kits and postpartum resources, following a similar partnership with Palomar Hospital. This represents a modest but concrete deployment of a maternal health product at named health systems, warranting a middling score for this beat.

scored.title: Navigating fairness in artificial intelligence-based prediction models: theoretical constructs and practical applications.
scored.why: This Viewpoint reviews 27 fairness definitions for artificial intelligence (AI)-based prediction models and argues for prioritizing clinical utility, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-based performance, calibration, and statistical parity as practical group-based metrics, illustrated through two use cases rather than new empirical data. It is a conceptual framework paper without novel validation or a clinical outcome, useful for framing bias-mitigation discussions but not a finding that changes practice on its own.

scored.title: The consensus-based CINEX guideline for reporting clinical information extraction studies.
scored.why: This paper presents CINEX, a consensus-based reporting guideline for clinical information extraction (IE) studies using large language models (LLMs) and other natural language processing methods, developed through a three-round Delphi process with 20 international experts resulting in 29 checklist items. It is a methodological standards document rather than a clinical evaluation or new capability, useful for future study design but not itself a finding about AI performance or patient care.

scored.title: Exploring Perceptions of Leveraging AI to Improve Outcomes in Maternal, Sexual, and Reproductive Health in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploratory Qualitative Study.
scored.why: This exploratory qualitative study gathered perceptions of AI's potential in maternal, sexual, and reproductive health (MSRH) from 59 stakeholders in sub-Saharan Africa via interviews and focus groups, framed using diffusion of innovations theory. It reports attitudes and hopes rather than any deployed AI system or measured outcome, so it offers limited actionable evidence for this reader despite touching the reproductive health beat.

scored.title: Data-driven insights in menopause: A scoping review of sensors and AI.
scored.why: This scoping review synthesized 58 studies on sensor and artificial intelligence (AI)-based approaches for monitoring menopause symptoms, finding heterogeneous sensing modalities and concluding that progress is limited by small datasets, inconsistent validation, and a near-exclusive focus on vasomotor symptoms. As a review with no new data or evaluated tool, it maps the landscape but offers no finding that would change clinical practice.

scored.title: Bridging the Diagnostic Gap: Reviewing Current Endometriosis Screening Tools and Models.
scored.why: This scoping review synthesized 18 studies on endometriosis screening tools, categorizing them into questionnaire-based, app-based, machine learning and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven, and subtype-focused models, reporting area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values from 0.77 to 0.95 with AI-driven models scoring highest. As a review it identifies gaps in external validation and cultural adaptation but presents no new evaluated tool or clinical outcome data.

scored.title: Causal associations between hormone replacement therapy and brain structure: Evidence from large-scale Mendelian randomization and double machine learning.
scored.why: Using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and Double Machine Learning (DML) on UK Biobank genetic and imaging data, this study found causal associations between hormone replacement therapy (HRT) timing and use with several brain structure measures, including white matter microarchitecture and cortical thickness. While the causal inference framework is methodologically rigorous, the outcomes are structural brain imaging phenotypes rather than clinical endpoints, and machine learning here serves as a statistical validation tool rather than a diagnostic or predictive clinical application.

scored.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Multi-Omics Biomarker Discovery in Ectopic Pregnancy: A Comprehensive Review.
scored.why: This narrative review synthesized 52 studies from 1988-2026 on artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and multi-omics approaches for ectopic pregnancy diagnosis and management, reporting area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values up to 0.929 for methotrexate failure prediction. As a review of prior retrospective, mostly single-center studies without new data or prospective validation, it highlights promising directions but no finding ready to change practice.

scored.title: Interobserver and intraobserver variability of fetal and maternal Doppler measurements: systematic review and meta-analysis.
scored.why: This systematic review and meta-analysis pooled 26 studies to quantify interobserver and intraobserver variability of umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, and uterine artery Doppler measurements using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), finding generally poor-to-moderate reproducibility by strict criteria. Artificial intelligence is mentioned only as a future direction to improve measurement standardization, so this is primarily a methodologic quality study rather than an AI evaluation.

scored.title: Identification of genomic features that uniquely impact estrogen receptor alpha binding and its effects on gene expression in endometrial cancer.
scored.why: This study used machine learning on genomic data from endometrial and breast cancer cell lines to identify transcription factors, such as SOX17 in endometrial cells, that predict estrogen receptor (ER) binding and gene regulation, confirmed with a CRISPR knockout screen. This is a mechanistic molecular biology study using machine learning as an analytic tool rather than a clinically applied prediction model, so its direct relevance to the reader's clinical AI or reproductive health beats is limited.

scored.title: Effects of a Safety User Interface Bundle on Verification Intentions in Generative AI Chat Use Among Older Chinese Adults: Randomized Vignette Survey.
scored.why: This randomized vignette survey tested whether adding safety user interface (UI) cues to a generative AI chat system increased verification intention among 200 older Chinese adults, finding a statistically significant but small increase (adjusted beta 0.293 on a 7-point scale) without harming reliance intention. The study concerns general AI trust calibration in everyday information seeking rather than clinical patient-provider communication, limiting its direct relevance to this reader's focus on patient-facing medical AI.

scored.title: Comparison of responses from google and large language models to the top frequently asked questions on lumbar spinal stenosis: an evaluation of accuracy and completeness.
scored.why: This study compared responses from Google Search, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity to eight frequently asked patient questions about lumbar spinal stenosis, with orthopedic spine surgeons rating accuracy and completeness on Likert scales; Gemini scored highest but no pairwise difference reached the predefined minimal clinically important difference (MCID) threshold of 1.0 point. This is a routine comparison of chatbot outputs against a rubric with expert raters rather than against real clinician-delivered care, and the authors themselves note the differences, while statistically significant, were not clinically meaningful.

scored.title: Exploring Perceptions of Leveraging AI to Improve Outcomes in Maternal, Sexual, and Reproductive Health in Sub-Saharan Africa: Exploratory Qualitative Study.
scored.why: This exploratory qualitative study gathered perceptions of AI's potential in maternal, sexual, and reproductive health (MSRH) from 59 stakeholders in sub-Saharan Africa via interviews and focus groups, framed using diffusion of innovations theory. It reports attitudes and hopes rather than any deployed AI system or measured outcome, so it offers limited actionable evidence for this reader despite touching the reproductive health beat.

scored.title: Reliability and readability of Artificial Intelligence generated information on acute cholecystitis: A comparative analysis.
scored.why: This comparative study assessed reliability and readability of AI-generated information on acute cholecystitis (AC) across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity in Spanish and English, using validated readability formulas and reviewer-rated reliability scores, finding no significant reliability differences but notable readability variation between tools. This is a routine chatbot benchmarking exercise without any clinician comparator or patient outcome measure, placing it in the low-value tier for this discriminating beat.

scored.title: Quantifying the Intensity of Online Social Support via Large Language Model-Based Evidence Extraction: Development and Validation Study.
scored.why: This study developed a deep learning model combined with a large language model (LLM) to extract evidence and quantify the intensity of informational and emotional support in online mental health forum posts, achieving moderate accuracy (0.598 to 0.728) across two annotated datasets. This is a natural language processing methods study on peer support forums rather than clinician or patient-facing medical communication, making it only loosely related to this reader's beat on LLMs talking to or about patients.

scored.title: The Understandability and Readability of Online Patient Education Materials and ChatGPT Responses Regarding Xerostomia.
scored.why: This study assessed readability and understandability of online patient education materials versus ChatGPT responses about xerostomia using standard readability scores (Flesch Kincaid Grade Level, Flesch Reading Ease) and the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT), finding ChatGPT text was less readable than existing web sources. This is a routine readability benchmark without any clinician comparator or patient outcome measure, fitting the low-priority pattern for this beat.

scored.title: Enriching Clinical Trials With Machine Learning.
scored.why: This JAMA piece on enriching clinical trials with machine learning has no abstract or text provided, so no methodology or findings can be assessed. Without substantive content, it cannot be judged as a meaningful contribution to clinical artificial intelligence (AI) this week.

scored.title: Global advances in health artificial intelligence: a workforce imperative.
scored.why: This Lancet piece is a commentary arguing that clinical artificial intelligence (AI) tools like ambient documentation and inbox triage should be framed as workforce retention strategies rather than replacements, citing a projected shortfall of 11 million health professionals by 2030. It presents no new data, trial, or deployment result, functioning as policy opinion rather than evidence that would change practice.

scored.title: From pixels to patterns: the AI revolution in stem cell-derived models.
scored.why: This Nature Methods Perspective surveys how artificial intelligence (AI), including convolutional neural networks and foundation models, is being applied to image-based analysis of stem cell-derived organoids and embryo models, without presenting new experimental data or clinical validation. It is a review of basic developmental biology tools, several steps removed from patient-facing reproductive medicine and offers no evaluable clinical finding.

scored.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy reduces regulatory T-cells in cervical cancer.
scored.why: This study used ImmuNet, a validated machine-learning image analysis platform, to quantify immune cell changes in cervical cancer tumors before and after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT), finding reduced regulatory T-cell (Treg) density and an association between lower post-treatment Treg proliferation and better overall survival (OS). The core contribution is immunological and clinical, with the AI tool serving only as a cell-counting instrument rather than the focus of evaluation, limiting its relevance to a clinical AI or reproductive AI beat.

scored.title: Integrative computational toxicology and experimental validation unveils ESR1-mediated steroidogenic disruption in triphenyl phosphate-induced female reproductive toxicity.
scored.why: This preclinical toxicology study used machine learning to prioritize ESR1 among candidate genes linking triphenyl phosphate (TPHP) exposure to female reproductive toxicity, supported by transcriptomics, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments in ovarian cell lines. The machine learning component is a target-prioritization step within a mechanistic toxicology pipeline, not a clinical or diagnostic AI application relevant to patient care.

scored.title: Artificial intelligence must not worsen maternal health inequalities.
scored.why: This J R Soc Med piece argues that artificial intelligence (AI) must not worsen maternal health inequalities, but no abstract or text is provided, so its argument, evidence, or specific recommendations cannot be assessed. scored.title: Antibiotic mixture exposure in meconium affects child neurodevelopment via altering early-life gut microbiome and metabolome.
scored.why: This cohort study of 300 mother-infant pairs used machine learning within a broader multi-omics analysis to link meconium-measured antibiotic burden with lower neurodevelopmental scores at 6 months, mediated by gut microbiome and metabolome changes. The machine learning component is an analytical tool embedded in an environmental epidemiology study rather than a clinical AI application, and the findings are explicitly hypothesis-generating pending replication.

scored.title: [Clinical and preprocedural factors influencing in vitro fertilization outcomes: a machine learning-based analysis].

It contains no patient-facing language model evaluation and is a review rather than new evidence, so it offers little for a reader tracking language models in patient communication.

scored.title: Ethical aspects of artificial intelligence use in neonatal intensive care units: a scoping review.
scored.why: This scoping review maps ethical, legal, and implementation issues in artificial intelligence (AI) use within neonatal intensive care units (NICUs) across 31 included sources, identifying eight recurring domains such as data governance, bias, and parental engagement. It is a qualitative synthesis of existing literature rather than new clinical evidence or an evaluation of any specific AI system, so it offers limited actionable content for this reader.

scored.title: ChatGPT and Large Language Models in Contemporary Nursing.
